title: Star trails over La Silla
caption: Star trails over La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Stars sweep across the sky in long trails above ESO's La Silla Observatory. The picture was made by combining a series of night-time exposures and was taken by ESO Photo Ambassador Alexandre Santerne.

The trails are a record of the sky's apparent daily motion. The stars are not really racing overhead. Instead, Earth turns on its own axis, carrying the observatory and the camera with it, so from the ground every star seems to move steadily across the sky over the course of the night.

Each exposure catches the stars in a slightly different position. Stacking many of them together joins those positions into continuous arcs. The result shows the sky's rotation in a single frame, something no one could see by simply looking up. Every trail is the path of one star, drawn by the turning of our own planet rather than by any motion of the star itself.

understand.summary: This is a stack of night-time photographs taken in visible light with a camera at La Silla. The exposure settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as fixed points. Only by combining many exposures can a camera record their motion as trails.

explore: The shape of star trails depends on where the camera points. Toward a celestial pole they curl into circles, while toward the celestial equator they become nearly straight lines. The caption does not say which way this camera pointed.
